claim: TileLang's sparse MLA backward is 'the sole hotspot of the GLM-5 DSA (DeepSeek Sparse Attention) training backward path' and is profiled on H200 (sm_90), with no sm_80 path or benchmark.
stance_target: cc-4's claim that the training-capable DSA backward is Hopper-or-newer
scope_conditions: TileLang PR #2592, merged 2026-07-22; ncu profiling on H200 sm_90; DQKV=576, DV=512, topk=2048, bf16
quoted_support: This operator is the sole hotspot of the GLM-5 DSA (DeepSeek Sparse Attention) training backward path (SparseMLA.autograd.Function), computing sparse MLA gradients for the latent geometry (DQKV=576, DV=512, topk=2048). ncu profiling on H200 (sm_90) shows it is severely memory-pipe bound

claim: The kernel is memory-pipe bound rather than DRAM bound (L1/TEX ~81-83% SOL, DRAM <1%, occupancy pinned at ~12.2% by registers and shared memory), so its performance lever is in-flight cp.async bytes, not bandwidth.
scope_conditions: ncu on H200, default deepseek_v32 shape H=64, block_H=64
quoted_support: L1/TEX ≈ 81–83% SOL, DRAM < 1%, achieved occupancy ≈ 12.2% (structurally pinned by registers + shared memory)

claim: Under tensor parallelism >= 2 the head count shrinks below block_H=64 and the 256-thread tier no longer applies, so the kernel's best configuration requires TP=1 (no attention-head split).
stance_target: How the sparse-MLA backward interacts with TP on this box
quoted_support: TP1 (no head split) benefits most ... TP ≥ 2: H shrinks, block_H < 64 forces the 128-thread fallback, so this lever no longer applies
